title: Beatrix and the Prom
premise: Ulyana Montrose has survived four years of being the only out kid in Hollow Creek by keeping her head down, but a forced senior project partner—the school board president's golden-boy son, Theo Vance—drags her into the open when they uncover records showing the district quietly expelled a trans student years ago and paid off his family. As they dig deeper, Ulyana realizes the buried student was her own older brother, whose 'move to Seattle' was a lie her parents still maintain. With graduation looming and the school board moving to seal the archives permanently, Ulyana must choose between protecting her family's fragile peace and burning the truth into public view—at prom, in front of everyone.
about_author: Odile Sterling is a former small-town debate coach who writes about kids who refuse to wait politely for permission. She lives in a house full of yearbooks she bought secondhand from towns that no longer have bookstores.

chapters.title: Nine Hundred Witnesses
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Senior spring begins; she maps the social geography of Hollow Creek High like a survival guide, counting days to graduation. A hallway incident forces her to perform 'fine' one more time. Emotional beat: weary resignation sharpening into quiet defiance.

chapters.title: Assigned
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Mr. Okafor pairs her with Theo Vance for the semester civics project on 'local institutional history.' Their first library session is all barbed politeness until Theo mentions offhand that the school archive room is locked and nobody knows why. Beat: reluctant curiosity replacing hatred.

chapters.title: The Locked Room
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They charm a janitor into opening the archive and find a gap in the enrollment records—a student excised mid-junior-year, 2019. Theo recognizes the settlement letterhead as his father's law firm. Beat: the thrill of discovery curdling into dread.

chapters.title: What the House Keeps
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. At home, she finds her mother's hidden box: a name, Eli Montrose, and a nondisclosure agreement. Her parents refuse to talk. Beat: betrayal—the enemy isn't only the school; it's the silence she was raised inside.

chapters.title: Truce Terms
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo confronts his father, gets stonewalled, and comes back to Ulyana offering a real alliance. They divide the work: he pulls financial records, she tracks down Eli's old friends online. Beat: guarded trust becoming something warmer neither will name.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Left
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She reaches Eli through an old classmate and they video-call; he confirms everything but begs her not to reopen it—he built a life by burying this town. Beat: grief and fury colliding; justice suddenly has a face that says no.

chapters.title: Sealed
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The board announces an 'archival modernization' that will digitize-and-destroy paper records before graduation. Theo's father threatens his college funding. Someone keys Ulyana's locker with a slur. Beat: the walls closing in, stakes turning physical.

chapters.title: Everything We Buried
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ulyana chooses truth over family peace and tells her parents she knows; her mother finally breaks, confessing she signed to protect Eli from worse. Ulyana realizes exposure must be undeniable and unignorable—one night, one audience. Beat: resolve hardening into strategy.

chapters.title: Prom
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At prom, under the gymnasium lights, Ulyana takes the microphone during the court announcement and reads Eli's name, the settlement, the NDA—while Theo live-streams the archived documents from the AV booth. The room splits between jeers and standing ovation. Beat: triumphant, terrifying climax.

chapters.title: Graduation Day
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Aftermath: a state investigation opens, the superintendent resigns, Eli calls home for the first time in five years. Ulyana walks across the stage not invisible but known—and chooses which parts of herself to carry forward. Beat: bittersweet, earned hope.
